decisions.reason: Changing the NFT standard to ERC-721C does not alter the use of IPFS and Pinata or the client's ability to remove the hosted ebook copy.
The token-standard decision does not change the optional offline PDF download or its email-certificate presentation.
The read-only PDF.js viewer and its entry points remain valid unchanged under ERC-721C.
The candidate already has a complete message-241 MODIFY recording ERC-721C, OpenSea Creator Controls, and marketplace whitelisting for enforcement of the $10 royalty.
The NFT-standard change does not necessarily alter any current metadata attribute or the existing pointer to the ownership-gated viewer.
The About page does not currently assert a specific ERC-721 standard, and the source does not require adding that technical detail to its copy.
The FAQ's existing Base, pricing, and royalty explanations remain correct; the source does not require FAQ copy about ERC-721C or marketplace whitelisting.
Selecting ERC-721C for royalty enforcement does not change the amount, trigger, recipient, or automatic payout of direct referral commissions.
The no-referral commission allocation remains a $5 payment to a random existing NFT holder regardless of the selected NFT standard.
The no-referral Small Block ticket recipient rule is unaffected by the ERC-721C royalty-enforcement decision.
ERC-721C marketplace controls constrain where royalty-enforced sales occur but do not change which book access, referral code, badges, or active ticket state transfers to a secondary buyer.
The NFT-standard and secondary-marketplace decision does not change Chainlink VRF selection, eligible ticket holders, weighting, or verification.
